LESSON: COMPASS DIRECTION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments Compass Direction (6 lessons) Location a
Topic 1.1: Compass Direction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Compass Direction. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can we show direction of places?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the four cardinal points of a compass
2. use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the four cardinal points of a compass
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the four cardinal points of a compass. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map
   In simple words: practise until you can use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Compass Direction using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Compass Direction in the examples.
2. Explain Compass Direction to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Compass Direction.
4. Show that you can: identify the four cardinal points of a compass

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Compass Direction using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Compass Direction important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Draw and label the four cardinal points, practise giving directions to places using the four cardinal points,
2. Digital Literacy: Learners interact with digital devices as they play computer games on compass direction for enjoyment.
3. Learning to learn: Learners develop relationships as they share resources and practise giving direction of places using the four cardinal points. 2 Values:
4. Unity: Learners cooperate as they practise giving direction of places using the four cardinal points.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the four cardinal points of a compass
2. use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
